**Draft:** The passage is mostly clean. It has specific details (31 years, lab stools, taps, the drive home) and a real voice. I changed the curly apostrophes to straight ones and tightened "I found myself doing the usual things" to a direct statement. The three cleaning tasks are concrete actions, so I kept them.

**Remaining patterns:** The three-item list of tasks is still a triad, but each item is a different action. The closing "I was ready to go, but I took my time" is a real mixed feeling, not a staged contrast, so it stays.

<final>
On my last day at Lakeview High, after 31 years of teaching chemistry, I did the usual things: straightened the lab stools, checked the taps, wiped down a bench that was already clean. I had spent so long thinking about retirement as a date on the calendar that I hadn't given much thought to how I would actually leave the room. Some lessons had gone beautifully; others I'd spent the drive home trying to figure out how to teach again. There were students I still wondered about, and a few whose questions had changed the way I explained something for the next twenty years. I was ready to go, but I took my time gathering my things.
</final>
